author: ohtadmin
title: Samuel A. Manchester
text:
Samuel A. Manchester, born March 26, 1947, in Newport, R.I., passed away peacefully Oct. 1, 2025, surrounded by his loving family.
A dedicated U.S. Navy veteran, he served his country proudly and later became a valued member of the American Legion.
For many years, Sam worked as a painter and sandblaster at General Dynamics Electric Boat at Quonset Point, where he made significant contributions before retiring. His commitment to his work was matched only by his dedication to his family and community.
Sam also was an active member of the former Portuguese American Citizens Club in Jamestown, where he found joy playing shuffleboard with friends and neighbors.
He is survived by his step-children, Frank E. Morse and his wife Lillian, Ritchie F. Morse and his wife Leslie, Randy A. Morse and his wife Debra and Tammy L. Olszewski and her husband Frank; and step-daughter-in-law, Holly Morse.
Sam cherished his large family, which includes 19 grandchildren, 30 great-grandchildren, and 14 great-great-grandchildren, all of whom were a great source of pride and happiness in his life.
Sam was preceded in death by his beloved parents, Carlton T. Sr. and Ruth E. (Parker) Manchester, and his devoted wife, Barbara (Ames) Morse-Manchester.
He also is mourned by his stepdaughters, Brenda F. Crawley and her husband Ronald and Donna M. Hanks and her husband Michael, as well as his step-son, Robert E. Morse.
A graveside service with military honors will be conducted at 11 a.m. Oct. 10, 2025, at Cedar Cemetery in Jamestown.
In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to American Legion Charities, P.O. Box 361626, Indianapolis, IN 46236.
Visit NardolilloFH.com for online condolences.
